item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-3a2f51717bd01e5a","start_unit":2,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"The Ministry of Finance reported that 2023 fiscal policy generated more than 2.2 trillion yuan in combined tax cuts, fee reductions, tax rebates, and deferred payments; supported small and micro enterprises, manufacturing, employment, education, health care, pensions, disaster recovery, rural development, and ecological protection.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.6","5B.9","6B.1","6B.2","6B.6","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"2023 policy execution, reported March 2024","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes policy direction to the CCP Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core and to the State Council.","limitations":["Official self-report; attribution to Xi is institutional and not evidence of personal authorship of each measure."]},{"source_id":"SRC-3a2f51717bd01e5a","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"National general public-budget revenue reached 21.6784 trillion yuan, up 6.4 percent, while expenditure reached 27.4574 trillion yuan, up 5.4 percent; fiscal policy maintained a 3 percent deficit-rate target and added 1 trillion yuan in bonds for disaster recovery and risk reduction.","question_ids":["5B.3","5B.6","5B.9","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"2023","ruler_attribution":"Reported by the Ministry of Finance under central fiscal policy direction.","limitations":["The report notes recovery effects and a low comparison base; it does not establish Xi-specific causal responsibility."]},{"source_id":"SRC-3a2f51717bd01e5a","start_unit":4,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"Central departments applied a long-term austerity rule, reduced central-level official hospitality and related public-expense budgets by 20 percent compared with 2019, and linked quarterly evaluations of austerity performance to departmental budget allocations.","question_ids":["5B.5","5B.7","7B.9","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Implemented during 2023; comparison baseline 2019","ruler_attribution":"Presented as a central government and party financial-management directive.","limitations":["Official account does not independently verify compliance or savings quality."]},{"source_id":"SRC-3a2f51717bd01e5a","start_unit":9,"end_unit":10,"fact_summary":"Central basic-research spending was 866.5 billion yuan in 2023, up 6.6 percent; the government funded major projects and supported research in artificial intelligence, quantum computing, and brain science, while raising the R&D tax deduction for integrated-circuit and industrial-machine-tool firms to 120 percent.","question_ids":["1B.7","1B.9","5B.1","5B.6","8B.2","8B.3","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"2023","ruler_attribution":"Officially framed as implementation of Xi Jinping-era national innovation and technological self-reliance priorities.","limitations":["The source reports inputs and programs, not independent evidence of research quality or catastrophic-risk safeguards."]},{"source_id":"SRC-3a2f51717bd01e5a","start_unit":11,"end_unit":16,"fact_summary":"The government reported 2023 increases in education, pensions, social assistance, public-health funding, health-insurance subsidies, disaster relief, and emergency preparedness, including 41.242 trillion yuan in education spending, 1,566.83 billion yuan for assistance to people in difficulty, 725.09 billion yuan for basic public-health services, and 384 billion yuan for resident medical-insurance subsidies.","question_ids":["6B.1","6B.2","6B.3","6B.6","6B.9","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"2023","ruler_attribution":"Reported as implementation of central government priorities under Xi-centered party leadership.","limitations":["Figures are official administrative outputs; independent incidence and service-quality evidence is not supplied."]},{"source_id":"SRC-3a2f51717bd01e5a","start_unit":25,"end_unit":30,"fact_summary":"Fiscal authorities reported a package for local-government debt risk: monitoring systems, stricter budget constraints, prohibition of new hidden debt, public exposure of eight accountability cases, inspections of major financial cases, performance evaluations, and integrated budget-management systems covering central and local budget units.","question_ids":["5B.3","5B.5","5B.7","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","8B.5","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Implemented or reported in 2023","ruler_attribution":"Presented as implementation of decisions by the CCP Central Committee and State Council.","limitations":["The same report acknowledges continuing irregular borrowing, inefficient fund use, and incomplete implementation in some localities."]},{"source_id":"SRC-fbcd03cbdb99f6ed","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"A peer-reviewed study using panel data from 30 Chinese provinces found that local-official corruption expanded local-government debt by impairing government-investment efficiency; it also found that the anti-corruption campaign supported debt management, especially in developed regions.","question_ids":["5B.5","5B.7","7B.9","8B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Study published 2023; empirical panel period is not specified in the supplied units","ruler_attribution":"The finding concerns China’s local-government system and anti-corruption campaign, not a quantified personal act by Xi.","limitations":["The supplied abstract does not provide the study years, effect sizes, or a direct Xi-level causal estimate."]},{"source_id":"SRC-f0a32f47e9785699","start_unit":4,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"On 4 June 2023, Beijing tightened access to Tiananmen Square and Hong Kong police detained at least 18 people around the anniversary of the 1989 crackdown; commemorations, related discussion, and books or memorial objects had been suppressed, while authorities continued to reject accountability for the killings.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","3B.8","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"2023","ruler_attribution":"The report describes actions by Chinese central and Hong Kong authorities under the Xi-led political system.","limitations":["The article reports events and statements but does not establish a personal order from Xi for each detention."]},{"source_id":"SRC-dd106f200264c2c9","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"Freedom House rated China’s internet freedom 9/100 and “Not Free,” calling it the world’s worst abuser of internet freedom for the ninth consecutive year; it reported censorship, legal and extralegal reprisals, AI-tool restrictions, and further consolidation of personal power by Xi after his third party-leader term.","question_ids":["4B.2","4B.3","4B.5","4B.6","4B.9","7B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Coverage period June 2022-May 2023, published 2023","ruler_attribution":"Freedom House directly links the consolidation and increasing repression to Xi’s leadership and the CCP.","limitations":["The assessment covers a period extending before and beyond calendar 2023 and uses an advocacy organization’s methodology."]},{"source_id":"SRC-dd106f200264c2c9","start_unit":17,"end_unit":20,"fact_summary":"Authorities systematically deleted online comments about approval of Xi’s third presidential term; nearly 20 percent of a sample of 4,170 dissent-related Sina Weibo posts were removed; censorship also covered zero-COVID criticism, pandemic deaths, Tiananmen discussion, minority issues, and LGBT and feminist content.","question_ids":["3B.3","3B.8","3B.9","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.1","7B.2"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Mostly 2022-2023 coverage period","ruler_attribution":"The source identifies state and CCP censorship institutions operating within Xi’s leadership system.","limitations":["The sample and reported removals do not quantify all censorship or prove Xi personally directed each deletion."]},{"source_id":"SRC-dd106f200264c2c9","start_unit":22,"end_unit":22,"fact_summary":"In February 2023, Chinese regulators told technology firms to discontinue access to ChatGPT and disclose plans for domestic AI chatbots; Chinese chatbots reportedly refused questions about Xi, and ChatYuan’s founder described layered keyword filtering.","question_ids":["1B.9","3B.5","4B.9","7B.1","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"2023","ruler_attribution":"The measures were issued by Chinese regulators within the Xi-led state and censorship system.","limitations":["The source does not establish whether the restrictions were intended as catastrophic-risk safeguards, political censorship, or both."]},{"source_id":"SRC-dd106f200264c2c9","start_unit":30,"end_unit":31,"fact_summary":"Chinese internet-censorship rules were described as arbitrary, opaque, lacking formal appeals, and immune from court challenge; December 2022 rules required platforms to review social-media posts before publication, while 2023 generative-AI rules required outputs to embody “core socialist values” and avoid politically disfavored information.","question_ids":["3B.4","3B.5","4B.4","4B.6","4B.9","7B.6","7B.7","8B.2"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Rules in force or issued during the 2022-2023 coverage period","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the regulatory system to the CAC and CCP-linked bodies consolidated under Xi’s tenure.","limitations":["The source is an external country assessment and does not provide a complete legal analysis of every rule."]},{"source_id":"SRC-dd106f200264c2c9","start_unit":46,"end_unit":47,"fact_summary":"During late-2022 zero-COVID protests, thousands mobilized through social media; authorities removed protest posts, restricted searches, detained scores of protesters, and ordered platforms to increase censorship, although the protests pressured the government into withdrawing the zero-COVID policy.","question_ids":["3B.8","3B.9","4B.3","4B.9","8B.8","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Events in late 2022 with consequences during the 2023 coverage period","ruler_attribution":"The source attributes censorship and policy reversal to Chinese authorities under Xi’s administration.","limitations":["The report does not establish whether the policy reversal was an intentional correction based on evidence or a response to political pressure."]},{"source_id":"SRC-dd106f200264c2c9","start_unit":52,"end_unit":55,"fact_summary":"During the coverage period, online dissent led to arrests and imprisonment, including a three-year sentence for a Uyghur student, seven years for blogger Ruan Xiaohuan, 14 years for lawyer Xu Zhiyong, and three and a half years for lawyer Chang Weiping; a man was also detained in May 2023 after allegedly using ChatGPT to generate false news.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.8","4B.3","4B.9","7B.6","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"2022-2023 coverage period; several sentences occurred in 2023","ruler_attribution":"The cases involved Chinese courts, police, and security institutions within the Xi-led system.","limitations":["The source summarizes reported cases and does not provide complete case files or adjudication records."]},{"source_id":"SRC-dd106f200264c2c9","start_unit":58,"end_unit":60,"fact_summary":"China imposed extensive real-name and identity requirements for online services; in December 2022 ISPs were required to discontinue service to unauthenticated users, and in February 2023 Apple removed the encrypted anonymous-account app Damus from China’s app store at the CAC’s request.","question_ids":["3B.5","4B.9","7B.6","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Measures in force or implemented during the 2022-2023 coverage period","ruler_attribution":"The measures were attributed to Chinese regulators and security laws under Xi-era governance.","limitations":["The source does not quantify enforcement across all providers."]},{"source_id":"SRC-dd106f200264c2c9","start_unit":63,"end_unit":67,"fact_summary":"China’s surveillance system was used after the 2022 protests to identify and arrest protesters; surveillance data included communications, location, facial-recognition and Wi-Fi information, while laws required companies to assist security agencies and retain user data without judicial oversight; a new national data bureau was announced in March 2023.","question_ids":["3B.5","3B.8","3B.9","4B.9","7B.6","7B.7","8B.2","8B.3"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"2023 reporting on systems used during 2022-2023","ruler_attribution":"The source describes national surveillance and data-governance institutions consolidated during Xi’s tenure.","limitations":["The report includes some earlier evidence and says a claim of deleting one billion records could not be independently verified."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a5457ee3d5eea54a","start_unit":3,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"UNODA reported that the United States alleged China had 500 operational nuclear warheads and that non-governmental sources assessed China was developing three new ICBM silo fields, new strategic delivery systems, a longer-range submarine-launched missile, an operational nuclear bomber mission, and a possibly nuclear-capable air-launched ballistic missile.","question_ids":["1B.1","1B.2","1B.5","1B.10","8B.3","8B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Developments reported for 2023","ruler_attribution":"The findings concern China’s state nuclear modernization under Xi’s leadership.","limitations":["The warhead estimate and capability assessments are attributed to external sources; China disputed the warhead allegation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a5457ee3d5eea54a","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"China rejected calls to announce a moratorium on fissile-material production for nuclear weapons, arguing that such moratoriums were unverifiable and unfairly biased toward larger nuclear-weapon States.","question_ids":["1B.4","1B.10","7B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"2023","ruler_attribution":"The position was advanced by the Chinese government in multilateral disarmament forums.","limitations":["The source does not identify the specific official who articulated the position or quantify its practical consequences."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a5457ee3d5eea54a","start_unit":30,"end_unit":30,"fact_summary":"The G20 New Delhi Declaration in September 2023 stated that the use or threat of use of nuclear weapons was inadmissible and that States must not use force to seek territorial acquisition; China participated in the G20 process.","question_ids":["1B.2","1B.4","1B.5","2B.7"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"September 2023","ruler_attribution":"China’s participation occurred under Xi’s government, but the supplied unit does not identify a personal Xi statement or decision.","limitations":["This is a multilateral declaration and does not prove implementation by China."]},{"source_id":"SRC-c95a4ea2291e817c","start_unit":2,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"A 2023 WorldCat record describes a two-volume official collection of Xi Jinping’s writings, covering November 2012-October 2022 and presenting Xi Jinping Thought as guidance for national modernization and national rejuvenation.","question_ids":["8B.1"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"Publication in 2023; contents cover 2012-2022","ruler_attribution":"Directly attributed to Xi Jinping’s published works and the official party-state framing.","limitations":["The catalog record supplies bibliographic description, not a dated 2023 policy act or implementation result."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":["SRC-4e2c80f5157af1d2","SRC-9f17f4b3764b71b7","SRC-4c9280aadc9204aa","SRC-c48fbcba1e0f304a","SRC-831b8c33b3c3770a"],"batch_limitations":["The Amnesty International document is a 2025 report and its supplied material does not provide a sufficiently bounded 2023 Xi-period fact for this batch.","The nuclear automation and cyber-wargaming articles report hypothetical scenarios or general research findings rather than concrete 2023 actions or institutional findings about Xi Jinping.","The Xi biography catalog record contains descriptive publication metadata but no concrete 2023 event, policy, quantitative result, or institutional finding beyond the existence and scope of the official collection."]}
